findings.quote: changes the reason of the `websocket.md` `app.ws("/chat", (req, ws) -> {` entry to ``app-defined types `ChatService` and `ChatMessage` ``, changes the reason of the `lifecycle.md` `RestApp app = RestApp.create();` entry to ``app-defined types `Database` and `UserService` `` ... and `./gradlew build` passes  /  (OPS-SSE-001 AC-4) ``app-defined types `Event` and `eventStore` ``
findings.description: The iter-2 fixes (A2-01, A2-05) introduced this. The verified test `DocsExamplesCompileTest#sdsAc12_OPS_HTTP_004_AC4_everySkipNamesFileBlockAndReason` (OPS-HTTP-004 AC-4, line 494) requires every skip reason to match `REASON` = `(later-wave method|illustrative copy of|absent type|app-defined type|app-defined variables?|app-defined methods) `[^`]+`.*` (lines 131-133). The plural `app-defined types `X`` does not match: after `app-defined type` the regex expects a space and a backtick, not `s`. I checked this with the same regex in Python: the plural form gives False and the singular form gives True. The existing entry `express-migration.md` already uses the singular form for two types (``app-defined type `TodoService` and `Todo` ``). As written, AC-6 makes the verified OPS-HTTP-004 test fail, so its own `./gradlew build passes` clause cannot hold. The OPS-SSE-001 AC-4 example has the same fault.
findings.suggested_fix: OPS-WS-001 AC-6: use ``app-defined type `ChatService` and `ChatMessage` `` and ``app-defined type `Database` and `UserService` ``, the singular form that the `REASON` pattern of OPS-HTTP-004 accepts. OPS-SSE-001 AC-4: use ``app-defined type `Event` and app-defined variable `eventStore` `` or ``app-defined type `Event` ``. If the plural should stay, AC-6 must instead say that `REASON` gains `app-defined types?` and that sdsAc12 keeps passing.

findings.quote: `cause` is `client` when the stream ended because a drain write or heartbeat to the socket failed with an `IOException` ... `shutdown` for the closing participant and for a stream force-closed by the adapter stop at the shutdown deadline ... Decision: ... an `IOException` on the socket always maps to `client`.
findings.description: The iter-2 fix (A2-03) introduced this. A stream force-closed at the deadline (FR-SSE-005 AC-5, FR-APP-020 AC-6) ends because TinyHttpd's `stop` calls `abortSocket()` on every remaining connection (HttpServer.stop, after the grace loop), so the blocked drain write throws an `IOException`. The same AC requires `cause=shutdown` for that stream and says that an `IOException` on the socket always maps to `client`. The same clash arises when a drain write fails with `IOException` after `close()` (`app`) or after an overflow end (`overflow`) was already recorded. A test of the force-closed stream therefore has no defined expected cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC-10: "the first end reason recorded wins: a stream already marked ended by `close()`, by overflow or by the closing participant keeps `app`, `overflow` or `shutdown` even when its drain write then fails with an `IOException`; only an `IOException` on a stream that was not yet marked ended maps to `client`". Add a TinyHttpd case asserting `cause=shutdown` for the stalled stream of FR-SSE-005 AC-5.

findings.quote: OPS-SSE-001 AC-4: "no `sse.md` skip reason names a wave 7 member (such as ``later-wave method `Response.sse()` `` or ``absent type `SseEvent` ``), which the `WAVE_SEVEN_MEMBERS` check of OPS-WS-001 AC-6 asserts"; OPS-WS-001 AC-6: "finds no skip reason naming a wave 7 member as a later-wave method"
findings.description: OPS-WS-001 AC-6 defines the check like the existing `waveSixMemberReasons`, which only scans `LATER_WAVE_NAMES` (`later-wave methods? `...``, DocsExamplesCompileTest:570). So it never sees the current reason ``absent type `SseEvent` `` (line 124). That block (`client.send(SseEvent.event("progress")...`) still fails to compile after wave 7 because `client` is undeclared in the `wrap()` stubs. A stale `absent type `SseEvent`` reason therefore survives both `sdsAc14_OPS_APP_002_AC2_everySkippedBlockStillFailsToCompile` and the planned check. OPS-SSE-001 AC-4 claims a guarantee that the check it cites does not give.
findings.suggested_fix: OPS-WS-001 AC-6: "... finds no skip reason naming a wave 7 member as a later-wave method or as an absent type". Alternatively, OPS-SSE-001 AC-4 names its own assertion that the sse.md `SseEvent` entry's reason is ``app-defined variable `client` ``.

findings.quote: AC-6: An exception thrown by an `onText` listener is passed to the `onError` listeners, logged at ERROR with the request id, and the client receives close `1011`
findings.description: Wave decision r2 W2-005 says that the core endpoint catches every exception from user code after `101`, and IR-WS-001 AC-1 declares `WebSocketHandler.handle(...) throws Exception`. The handler runs from the endpoint's `onOpen` (FR-WS-001 AC-3). No AC says what happens when the handler itself throws. TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener.onOpen` declares no checked exception, and its `run()` answers a `RuntimeException` from `onOpen` with `close(1011)` and a rethrow out of `handle`. So the result (1011 from the core, a TinyHttpd rethrow, or FR-WS-002 AC-9's ERROR log) is undefined and untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to FR-WS-006: "AC-10: a checked or unchecked exception thrown by the `ws` handler is caught by the core endpoint, passed to any `onError` listener the handler already registered, logged at ERROR with the request id, and closes the session with `1011`; `onClose` receives `1011` and no exception reaches TinyHttpd's `onOpen`, which an in-memory and a TinyHttpd test assert."

findings.quote: the `TestApp.webSocketRoute(path)` fixture is re-pointed to `app.ws`, and every test that uses it (StaticMethodTest, MiddlewarePipelineTest, ErrorPathTest, DefaultRestAppTest) still passes
findings.description: Verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-7 says that the test-fixtures harness uses the internal WebSocket-route hook to register a WebSocket-only route. Re-pointing `TestApp.webSocketRoute` to `app.ws` makes that clause untrue, and no wave 7 note records it as history, unlike FR-HTTP-022 AC-6. DefaultRestAppTest does not use the fixture: it calls `DefaultRestApp.webSocketRoute("/ws", h)` directly with a `RouteHandler` (lines 221, 240; FR-HTTP-008 AC-5/AC-7). The IR-WS-001 rationale also says this hook "becomes the implementation of `ws`", which would change its signature and break those two verified tests.
findings.suggested_fix: FR-WS-001 AC-7 / IR-WS-001 rationale: state that `DefaultRestApp.webSocketRoute(String, RouteHandler)` keeps its signature (the verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-5/AC-7 tests stay unchanged) and that FR-HTTP-008 AC-7's harness clause is history from wave 7, in the same way as the FR-HTTP-022 AC-6 note. Drop DefaultRestAppTest from the fixture-user list.

findings.quote: The `shutdown` steps of `docs/api/app.md` state, in this order: ... then `onStop`, closing owned resources and the logger flush as before
findings.description: `docs/api/app.md:217` says "timeout은 2단계(진행 중인 요청을 기다리는 시간)에만 걸리고". AC-8 reorders the steps (goodbye, then the wait, then force-close), and D-344/FR-APP-020 count the goodbye inside the deadline. That sentence then names the wrong step and leaves out the goodbye. AC-8 does not require it to be rewritten.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC-8: "and the sentence on what the timeout covers names the goodbye, the wait and the force-close steps by their new numbers while keeping that `onStop`, resource close and logger flush have no time limit".
